summary: Rigathi Gachagua served as the Deputy President of Kenya from September 2022 until his historic impeachment by the National Assembly and Senate in October 2024. His political career has been punctuated by high-profile legal battles over unexplained asset accumulation, tender allocations in Nyeri County, and constitutional impeachment charges regarding state resource allocation and regional rhetoric.
introduction: Rigathi Gachagua (born 28 February 1965) served as the Member of Parliament for Mathira Constituency (2017–2022) before being selected as William Ruto's running mate in the 2022 presidential election. As Deputy President, Gachagua spearheaded coffee and tea subsector reforms while publicly claiming government shareholding based on voting patterns. In October 2024, the National Assembly voted overwhelmingly (281 to 44) to impeach him on 11 constitutional charges including gross misconduct, stirring ethnic hostility, and amassing an unexplained Ksh 5.2 Billion wealth portfolio through corporate proxies during his two years in office. The Senate upheld five articles of impeachment on 17 October 2024, marking the first time in modern Kenyan history that a sitting Deputy President was removed by legislative trial.
